title: Robust early-warning canary + A/B framework for model versions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Deliver a production-ready A/B + canary framework that detects regressions early, limits user exposure, and automatically remediates via rollback or attenuation. This framework will support: staged canaries (attenuated traffic ramps), shadow traffic comparison, multi-variant A/B tests, cohort-aware exposure limits, and automated rollback governed by statistical checks and business-safety rules.

Scope:
- Experiment configuration UI + API (experiment definition, cohorts, hypothesis, primary/secondary metrics, ramp schedule).
- Exposure controller engine that enforces per-customer and global exposure quotas, supports attenuated routing (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%), and integrates with smart routing/fallback.
- Statistical evaluation layer: sequential checks, multiple-comparison correction, and optional Bayesian posterior checks.
- Auto-remediation actions: immediate rollback to previous stable model, pause/attenuate ramp, or divert to shadow-only for deeper inspection.
- Telemetry + dashboards: time-series for golden metrics, experiment-level drift, and a compact early-warning signal panel for on-call.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-running experimentation platform UI polish, user-facing cohort creation tools, and advanced causal inference analysis (these are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
- Experiment API exists (create/update/delete) and accepts: model_version, cohorts, primary_metric, safety_thresholds, ramp_schedule.
- Exposure controller enforces ramp schedule and per-identity caps; simulated load tests show <1% deviance from configured percentage.
- Statistical evaluator runs automated checks at each ramp step and emits pass/warn/fail decisions.
- Auto-rollback triggers when fail conditions are met and restores previous traffic split within 30s.
- Dashboards display experiment health, per-cohort metrics, and raw request/response drift for debugging.
- Runbook created and reviewed by SRE and Product; on-call acknowledged alerting thresholds.
- Security review completed for any data retention or signal export (KMS/HSM gating).
implementation_notes:
- Use existing routing hooks in runtime; add an ExposureController microservice to centralize ramp enforcement and quota bookkeeping.
- Statistical checks will be pluggable: start with sequential two-sample t-test / non-parametric and an optional Bayesian A/B option for teams that want probabilistic decisions.
- Implement a safeguard: require both statistical fail AND business-safety trigger (e.g., >2x error rate OR >5% drop in primary metric) for automatic rollback to avoid false positives.
- Shadow traffic comparisons to run in parallel path with identical inputs and hashing to cohort. Store mismatch buckets for later labeling/triage.
- Must include sampling hooks to limit telemetry retention costs (retain full traces for failures only).
metrics:
Primary metrics (per-experiment): latency p50/p95, top-level success rate (app-defined), quality proxy (e.g., rerank NDCG or task-specific score). Secondary metrics: error rate, cost per token, KV cache hit rate.
Statistical rules: sequential testing with alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) OR Bayesian posterior probability > 0.95 that new model is worse.
Multiple comparisons: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for experiments tracking >3 metrics.
Minimum sample size enforcement: experiments must collect N_min observations before any automated pass/fail decision (configurable per-metric).
rollout_plan:
1) Internal shadow run for 48h against production traffic subset (no user exposure). Validate data pipeline and drift signals.
2) Attenuated canary: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over configurable time windows (default 1h per step). Each step requires statistical/heuristic pass to progress.
3) If experiment flagged at any step: auto-attenuate to previous safe step and notify on-call via PagerDuty + Slack.
4) Post-rollout: keep canary in monitoring for 72h and run retrospective evaluation.
Rollback window: automated rollback must complete within 30s of trigger; manual rollback remain possible via Console with one-click action.
rollback_conditions:
Automated rollback if ANY of the following compound conditions are true: 
- Statistical fail: primary metric worse with p < 0.01 (sequential-corrected) OR Bayesian posterior P(new < old) > 0.95.
- Business-safety breach: error rate increases by >= 3x relative to baseline AND absolute error rate > 0.1%.
- Latency regression: p95 latency increase > 2x and absolute increase > 250ms.
- Spike in client-side complaints/alerts (integrated signal from support tooling).
Require at least one statistical condition AND one business-safety condition for auto-rollback unless 'panic-mode' flag is set for critical customers.
Rollback action: switch traffic routing to pinned stable model, mark experiment as failed, and create an auto-ticket (ENG) with diagnostics payload.
observability_and_alerting:
- Build an experiment health dashboard per-experiment with: live traffic split, primary/secondary metric timeseries, sequential test p-values / Bayesian posterior, latency heatmaps, and raw mismatch examples for shadow traffic.
- Alerts: warn at early-warning thresholds (e.g., metric delta > 10% but below rollback), critical when rollback thresholds met. Integrate with PD for P0 escalations.
- Traces: sample 1% of successful ops, 100% of failed ops during rollouts; store signed payload hashes only to avoid PII leakage.
- Cost telemetry: report per-experiment token cost and model utilization to the Console cost breakdown.
runbook_and_playbook:
- On alert: triage using experiment dashboard -> inspect mismatch bucket -> run A/B classifier on top 200 mismatched examples.
- If auto-rollback triggered: confirm rollback completed, notify product + eng leads, run postmortem template.
- If attenuated: increase observation window and require a manual approval to re-attempt ramp.
- Escalation matrix: on-call -> SRE lead -> Model owner -> PM.
- Postmortem template and RCA required for any auto-rollback.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: false positive rollbacks due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: require compound conditions (statistical + business).
Risk: signal leakage and privacy concerns from storing examples. Mitigation: hash inputs, only store examples when explicit consent or when sanitized, security review mandatory.
Risk: increased cost from shadow runs. Mitigation: sample shadow traffic adaptively and limit full trace retention.
Risk: rollout automation could mis-route traffic if routing hooks change. Mitigation: add end-to-end simulated canary tests to CI/CD.
